candidates.title: Anne Imhof: House of Swans
candidates.blurb: Anne Imhof's durational performance-installation arrives in Asia, reconfiguring Tai Kwun's colonial architecture into a live tableau of endurance and spectacle.
candidates.why_shortlisted: major European artist, first Asia institutional show

candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Kwade's mirrored pavilions bisect Tai Kwun's former prison yard, turning colonial stone into a study in reflection and perceptual distortion.

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: Met jewellery spanning 5,000 years examined through body modification and ornament, a rare museum loan that sidesteps the usual imperial narrative.
candidates.why_shortlisted: major Met loan, global jewellery cross-culturally

candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Egyptian state collections shown in Hong Kong for the first time, positioning HKPM as a conduit for non-Western antiquities beyond the Beijing axis.
candidates.why_shortlisted: rare Egyptian state loan to Asia, institutional diplomacy

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: Treasures of the Mughal Court from the Victoria and Albert Museum
candidates.blurb: V&A Mughal holdings read against Beijing imperial craft, a rare institutional dialogue that tests Hong Kong's claim to mediate East-South cultural exchange.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong's Venice Biennale pavilion restaged locally, testing whether the work holds without the validation architecture of the Giardini or Arsenale.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: HKMA's survey of local contemporary practice, notable for what it includes and what it diplomatically omits from the city's last decade of cultural production.
candidates.why_shortlisted: rare Hong Kong contemporary survey from public institution

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Muwen Tang's export-ware collection reframes Canton as the original intercultural workshop, Hong Kong's absent ancestor city finally foregrounded.
candidates.why_shortlisted: major private collection, Canton as trade-art origin

candidates.title: Joyful Encounters: The Connoisseurship and Art of Wong Kwan Shut
candidates.blurb: Hong Kong merchant-collector Wong Kwan Shut's dual practice as painter and acquirer, a study in literati connoisseurship adapted to mid-century trade capital.
candidates.why_shortlisted: local collector-artist, Hong Kong literati diaspora

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Expatriate collector Chris Hall's Chinese textiles, spanning 4,000 years, shown as an alternative social history told through weave structure and trade routes.
candidates.why_shortlisted: major private textile collection, material culture focus

candidates.title: Brilliance: Ming Dynasty Ceramic Treasures from the Palace Museum, 1368–1644
candidates.blurb: Long-term Ming ceramics installation testing whether extended display duration shifts visitor engagement from blockbuster spectacle to sustained study.

candidates.title: Heavenly Horses: Masterpieces from the Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Imperial horse portraiture as a proxy for frontier expansion and breeding diplomacy, a politically oblique subject read through aesthetic refinement.
